response.sql: WITH b AS (SELECT o.timespan, COUNT(DISTINCT o.recordvault) AS cnt FROM riskandmargin r JOIN orders o ON r.ordervault = o.recordvault GROUP BY o.timespan), s AS (SELECT timespan, cnt, cnt * 1.0 / SUM(cnt) OVER () AS share FROM b), a AS (SELECT timespan, cnt, share, AVG(share) OVER () AS avg_share FROM s) SELECT SUM(cnt) AS total_count, AVG(share) AS avg_share, AVG(share - avg_share) AS avg_excess FROM a WHERE share > avg_share

assumptions.assumption: Orders with a NULL timespan form one bucket, and GROUP BY puts all NULLs in a single group. The inner join drops risk/margin records that have no matching order.
The average of all bucket shares is taken over every bucket, including the NULL bucket, before filtering. The kept buckets are those whose share is strictly above that average.
Shares are computed with decimal division, not integer division, and nothing is rounded.
